title: Towards High Semantic Fidelity: Hyperdimensional Symbolic Messages in Multi-Agent Communication
claim: Existing message formats lose meaning in conversion and under noise; ours stays interpretable and keeps noisy samples clustered.
layout: 2 panels; left sender-to-receiver rows, right three t-SNE plots; smiley fidelity cues
description: The figure has two dashed-border panels. The left panel is about conversion fidelity. A robot Sender on the left branches into three rows: (a) numerical messages, (b) neural messages, and (c) the proposed symbolic messages. Each row has a small icon, a message format (a quantized vector Q, or a dense vector), and a yellow box showing the semantic content the receiver gets. Arrows lead to a robot Receiver on the right. Emoji faces mark quality: yellow for meh, red for bad, green for good. Row (a) gives a vague instruction, row (b) gives '???', and row (c) gives a structured, readable list. The right panel shows three t-SNE scatter plots with original and noisy samples. Numerical samples are scattered, neural samples form loose clusters, and the proposed method forms tight clusters. A legend and an orange '+ Noise' arrow sit at the bottom. The green smiley on the proposed method draws the eye first.
caption: Comparison of Semantic Fidelity of Messages. The left shows the conversion fidelity in terms of the embedding process, message format, and semantic content. The right employs t-SNE to exhibit their transmission fidelity when exposed to noise.
abstract: Semantic fidelity is essential for multi-agent communication under non-ideal channels, comprising transmission fidelity and conversion fidelity. Yet existing numerical and neural message formats cannot simultaneously achieve both. To address this, we propose a novel message format-\textbf{H}yperdimensional \textbf{S}ymbolic \textbf{M}essages (HSM) and its corresponding communication framework \textbf{Herm}. For transmission fidelity, Herm suppresses semantic entanglement via an entity-attribute-value structured encoding pipeline. For conversion fidelity, Herm first leverages a receiver-centric ego-binding mechanism to align semantics. Then, a similarity-aware dual-branch fusion module is proposed to prevent critical semantic dilution. To realize explicit message-semantic conversion, we devise an iterative decoding scheme via algebraic inverse operations. Experiments exhibit that Herm outperforms baselines across various noisy scenarios while maintaining superior structural readability.
